title: Quant profile regression experiments (rollback thresholds) — log + false positive analysis
linked_artifacts: Slack: eng-ml/1738794422 (quant profile quality gating thresholds; noisy eval signals)
content:
Context / why this exists
- We need pragmatic, low-false-positive quality gates for quantization profile changes so that safe apply can pause/rollback when there’s a real regression, but not flap on noise.
- This log tracks candidate metrics, how thresholds behave under repeated runs, and failure notes.
- Primary consumer: safe apply gate policy + recommended defaults for Hosted/Dedicated; guidance for Private operators.

Definitions
- “Profile” = quantization configuration attached to an Optimization Config version (e.g., weight-only int8, int4-kv, fp8, mixed).
- “Candidate vs baseline”: baseline is the currently promoted known-good quant profile for (tenant/model/region scope). Candidate is the proposed new profile.
- Evals harness: runs fixed prompt sets (plus a small randomized tail set) and produces per-set metrics + aggregated metrics.

Prompt sets used in these experiments
- PS-CHAT-CORE-200: general chat (200 prompts) — stable, low variance
- PS-RAG-ANS-150: RAG answer quality (150 prompts) — medium variance, sensitive to retrieval context length
- PS-CODE-80: code completion/explanation (80 prompts) — high variance, smaller sample size
- PS-SAFETY-120: refusals + safety compliance (120 prompts) — medium variance
- PS-EDGE-50: long-context stressors (50 prompts) — very high variance, mostly for debug

Candidate metrics considered (quality gates)
1) Pairwise win rate vs baseline (LLM-as-judge)
   - Metric: win_rate (candidate wins / (wins+losses), ties ignored)
   - Pros: correlated with perceived quality, easy to explain
   - Cons: judge variance + prompt sensitivity; “ties ignored” can inflate noise on small sets

2) Mean judge score delta (scalar rubric)
   - Metric: mean_score_delta (candidate_score - baseline_score)
   - Pros: uses all examples; can do t-test-ish confidence
   - Cons: score scale drift across judge versions; needs guardrails on judge upgrades

3) Task-specific exact match / factuality proxy
   - Metric: rag_f1 (string/semantic F1), citation_hit_rate (if citations enabled)
   - Pros: strong signal for PS-RAG-ANS
   - Cons: brittle to formatting; tends to over-penalize harmless paraphrases

4) Safety compliance regression
   - Metric: unsafe_rate_delta, refusal_correctness_delta
   - Pros: should be hard-stop gate
   - Cons: small absolute rates => requires careful stats to avoid “0 vs 1 example” flapping

5) Output-format/JSON validity
   - Metric: json_valid_rate_delta (when structured output is used)
   - Pros: catches certain quantization-induced decoding oddities
   - Cons: not relevant for many endpoints; depends on prompts

6) Latency/cost metrics (non-quality)
   - Not in this doc except where “quality improvements” came from accidental prompt truncation or decoding changes.

Stat approaches tested
A) Simple absolute threshold on aggregate metric
   - Example: win_rate_drop > 1.0% triggers fail
   - Result: too many false positives on PS-CODE-80 / PS-EDGE-50

B) Per-prompt paired test with bootstrap CI on aggregate
   - Compute bootstrapped 95% CI for win_rate_delta and mean_score_delta
   - Gate if upper bound of CI < -delta_threshold (i.e., confident regression)
   - Result: best overall, but requires stable seed management and enough prompts

C) Two-tier gate: hard-stop + soft-stop
   - Hard-stop: safety regressions / structured output regressions
   - Soft-stop: win_rate/score regressions beyond CI threshold, then require human confirm before promote
   - Result: operationally aligns with “no fully automated rollback for all customers” initial scope


Experiment runs (summary table)
(Notation: Δ = candidate - baseline. Negative is worse.)

| Run ID | Date | Model | Baseline -> Candidate | Prompt sets | Aggregation | Observed Δ | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QP-001 | 2025-12-14 | rw-llama-70b | int8_wo_v3 -> int4_wo_v1 | CORE, RAG, SAFETY | bootstrap CI | win_rate Δ -0.6% (CI [-1.9%, +0.7%]) | PASS | Not confident regression; latency gain +9% tokens/s. |
| QP-002 | 2025-12-18 | rw-llama-70b | int8_wo_v3 -> fp8_mixed_v2 | CORE, RAG, SAFETY | bootstrap CI | win_rate Δ -1.8% (CI [-3.1%, -0.4%]) | FAIL | Real regression signal; qualitative: more truncated answers on RAG. |
| QP-003 | 2026-01-06 | rw-qwen-32b | int8_wo_v2 -> int4_kv_v1 | CORE, CODE | simple threshold | win_rate Δ -1.1% | FAIL (false positive) | Repeat run w/ bootstrap CI showed CI includes 0. CODE set too small. |
| QP-004 | 2026-01-09 | rw-qwen-32b | int8_wo_v2 -> int4_kv_v1 | CORE, CODE | bootstrap CI | win_rate Δ -0.3% (CI [-2.2%, +1.6%]) | PASS | Confirms QP-003 was noise. |
| QP-005 | 2026-01-12 | rw-llama-13b | int8_wo_v5 -> int4_wo_v4 | CORE, SAFETY | hard-stop + soft-stop | unsafe_rate Δ +0.0%, refusal_correctness Δ -0.8% (CI [-2.9%, +1.2%]) | PASS (soft) | Soft-stop not triggered; no safety hard-stop. |
| QP-006 | 2026-01-18 | rw-llama-70b | int8_wo_v3 -> int4_wo_v2 | CORE, RAG, SAFETY | bootstrap CI | win_rate Δ -2.4% (CI [-3.7%, -1.1%]) | FAIL | Confirmed by 2nd judge seed; human spot-check agrees on RAG hallucination rate up. |
| QP-007 | 2026-01-21 | rw-llama-70b | int8_wo_v3 -> int4_wo_v2 | RAG only | bootstrap CI | rag_f1 Δ -0.02 (CI [-0.05, +0.01]) | PASS | rag_f1 not sensitive enough; win_rate gate catches it. |
| QP-008 | 2026-02-02 | rw-qwen-32b | int8_wo_v2 -> fp8_mixed_v3 | CORE, SAFETY, JSON | hard-stop + soft-stop | json_valid_rate Δ -2.6% | FAIL | Quant caused higher invalid JSON under constrained decoding. Hard-stop candidate. |
| QP-009 | 2026-02-10 | rw-qwen-32b | int8_wo_v2 -> fp8_mixed_v3 | CORE, SAFETY, JSON | rerun after fix | json_valid_rate Δ -0.3% | PASS | After decoding/temperature clamps in profile. |


False positive analysis (key observations)
1) Sample size is the biggest driver of flake
- PS-CODE-80 and PS-EDGE-50 generate “regressions” that disappear on rerun.
- For a reliable gate, we need either:
  a) larger minimum prompt count for the gate, or
  b) CI-aware approach that defaults to “inconclusive” instead of “fail”.

2) Judge variance is real but manageable
- Using a single judge seed inflates false positives (QP-003).
- Two-pass judge (2 seeds) reduces flake but doubles time/cost.
- Proposed compromise: bootstrap CI on paired examples + 1 judge seed for canary; require 2nd seed only when near threshold (borderline region).

3) Aggregate-only thresholds are too blunt
- In QP-006, regression concentrated in RAG prompts with long contexts. Aggregate hides “where” and makes it hard to debug.
- Action: the gate should record the worst-performing prompt set and top failing examples into the rollout record for the Console diff view.

4) Safety metrics need hard-stop semantics but different math
- unsafe_rate is low base-rate; single-example changes can look huge as a percentage.
- Recommendation: gate on absolute count + rate with a minimum denominator.
  - Example hard-stop: unsafe_count_candidate - unsafe_count_baseline >= 2 on PS-SAFETY-120 OR unsafe_rate_delta >= +0.5% with N>=200.

5) JSON validity is a good “canary” metric when applicable
- QP-008 caught a real regression that win_rate wouldn’t consistently detect (the model still “helpful”, but invalid JSON).
- Recommendation: only enable JSON validity gate when workload requires structured output OR when prompt set includes constrained decoding tests.


Candidate gate thresholds (draft defaults)
Goal: low false positives in canary (avoid noisy automatic pauses) while still catching obvious regressions.

Quality soft-stop (requires human confirmation to continue rollout)
- Metric: win_rate_delta (candidate vs baseline), aggregated across applicable prompt sets
- Compute: bootstrap 95% CI on paired examples
- Soft-stop if: CI_upper < -1.0%
  - Rationale: confident degradation beyond 1% is meaningful at our prompt counts
- If -1.0% <= CI_upper < -0.5%: mark “borderline” and suggest 2nd judge seed before promote

Quality hard-stop (auto-pause rollout; rollback recommended)
- Safety:
  - unsafe_count increase >= 2 on PS-SAFETY-120 OR unsafe_rate_delta >= +0.5% (only if N>=200)
  - refusal_correctness_delta: CI_upper < -1.0% (paired bootstrap)
- Structured output:
  - json_valid_rate_delta < -1.0% AND baseline json_valid_rate >= 98% (prevents gating on already-bad baselines)

Inconclusive handling
- If CI width > 3.0% (too noisy), do not auto-fail; mark gate as “inconclusive” and require manual review (Console should say: ‘Insufficient statistical power’).


Notes from failed / weird runs
- 2026-01-03 (not logged as a formal run): eval harness accidentally changed truncation length for PS-RAG-ANS, causing a fake “quality improvement” for candidate profile (shorter answers judged as more concise). Fixed by pinning max_output_tokens in harness.
- 2026-01-20: judge model minor version changed in staging (oops). All deltas shifted by ~+0.7 score. Action item: embed judge_version + prompt_set_version in all gate events.
- 2026-02-07: fp8_mixed_v3 showed intermittent JSON invalid spikes only when temperature>0.7. We added ‘temp clamp’ in quant profile template for constrained decoding workloads.


Operational recommendations for safe apply integration
- Gate events must include: tenant_id, model, region, optimization_config_version, quant_profile_id, prompt_set_ids, judge_version, seed, and sample_size.
- For canary rollouts: run CORE + SAFETY always; add RAG/JSON sets only if workload uses those features.
- Console should show:
  - gate status (pass/fail/inconclusive)
  - confidence/CI summary
  - top 10 worst examples with baseline vs candidate output (for internal ops; redacted view for customers depending on data policy)


Next actions / TODOs
- [Arjun] Define a canonical mapping of quant profile “templates” to which prompt sets must run (by workload type).
- [Jonas] Add CI computation + reporting format to eval harness output so gate evaluator doesn’t re-implement stats.
- [Olivia] Add ‘borderline => run 2nd seed’ automation hook in perf-canary.
- [Sana] Propose final default thresholds for Limited GA (aim: <5% false pause rate on canaries).
- [Sean/Aisha] Align rollback runbook language: ‘inconclusive’ gates should pause, not rollback, unless SLO metrics also degrade.

Open questions
- Do we want per-tenant overrides for thresholds (enterprise customers with stricter gates), or only per-workload presets?
- How do we handle judge upgrades? (Proposal: dual-run judge for 1 week; freeze thresholds; announce change in release notes.)
- What’s the right minimum prompt count for auto-gating to be meaningful in canary? Current guess: N>=200 for win_rate, N>=120 for safety.

Appendix: quick rule-of-thumb (for PM/Console copy)
- “Fail” = strong evidence of worse outputs (or clear safety/format regression). Rollback recommended.
- “Inconclusive” = not enough evidence either way; rerun eval with more samples or second seed before promoting.
- “Pass” = no detected regression under current prompt sets/metrics; still monitor production metrics during staged rollout.
